I prefer we implement a `LimitMinCapBuffer` and insert it between the level of `bytes.NewBuffer` and `CompressWriter`, so when `CompressWriter.Write` returns the written bytes less than expected or returns a specific error, we can rotate the upper writter.

maybe some logging libraries already have this technique?

> I prefer we implement a `LimitMinCapBuffer` and insert it between the level of `bytes.NewBuffer` and `CompressWriter`, so when `CompressWriter.Write` returns the written bytes less than expected or returns a specific error, we can rotate the upper writter.

I understand what you means. Can we merge this pr first as a bug fix and then file another issue as an improvement? Because for now the most important problem is that dumpling can work when upload compressed data to S3.

> where did we test that dumpling will generate files greater than 5MB?

We use this go file to import 50MB data into MySQL and dump them as one file in s3 test.
```bash
# load 50MB data into MySQL
(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && GO111MODULE=on go build -o out)
$DUMPLING_BASE_NAME/out -B $DB_NAME -T $TABLE_NAME -P 3306 -w 16
```

The file `prematch33517.active_event.000000000.sql.gz` which fails to close is about 35 MB size. 2 other files (sizes 2.7 GB and 379 MB) fail too.
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_UploadPart.html says "Each part must be at least 5 MB in size, except the last part. There is no size limit on the last part of your multipart upload."
This error occurs when one of the parts is less than 5MB in size and isn't the last part (the last part can be any size).
comments: We will check this soon. You can try without `-c gzip` which should be fine.
Yes, without `-c gzip` it is OK.

> @lichunzhu How to understand this error

External storage didn't calculate the compressed data's length correctly.
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments: can you explain more how this `continue` fix the error ? seems it just  save once `u.uploadChunk`

For normal files, writing n bytes means that `u.buf` will grow n bytes, so we can directly write chunkToFill bytes and u.buf can reach 5MB.
But for compressed files, writing n bytes means that `u.buf` will only grow m (m << n) bytes, now `u.buf` may still much less than 5MB, so we can upload here directly.
